purpose: Test whether a smaller start ritual reduces delay on a chosen writing project.
boundaries: Do not retain raw journal text

preferences.statement: The user prefers direct recommendations after a short context check.

goals.statement: Start the selected writing task on three planned weekdays.
goals.success_evidence: A timestamped five-minute start on three planned days.
goals.stop_condition: Pause if the plan displaces required sleep.

hypotheses.statement: The first-step ambiguity may contribute more to delay than lack of interest.
hypotheses.context_boundary: Only this writing project during the current work period.
supporting_evidence: The user reports starting more easily when the next paragraph is named.
disconfirming_or_missing_evidence: Energy and competing workload have not been compared.
alternatives: The task may be lower priority than the user wants to admit.
The planned time may conflict with energy.

experiments.question: Does naming the next five-minute action the night before reduce start delay?
experiments.action: On three planned nights, write one five-minute starting instruction for the next morning.
experiments.trigger: After closing the writing document for the day.
experiments.coping_response: If the instruction feels too large, reduce it to opening the file and adding one sentence.
experiments.evidence: Whether a five-minute start occurs and approximate delay after the planned start time.
experiments.stop_condition: Stop if it causes sleep loss or work-policy conflict.
